title: metadata-protocol: a by-name /meta read of a non-object item (app, view, page, …) serves a disabled package's item while the list omits it; #24097 closes the object half only
body:
**Filing gate ①**, class (b): one reader of a rule answers differently from another reader of the same rule. **`reach:`** a public door, measured over HTTP by #24097's dev (report 6238493670, out-of-scope finding 1) on `pnpm dev:crm -- --fresh` at objectstack `81e9289ba` (PR #24208's head; that PR does not touch the non-object by-name path). With the writable package `app.probe-24097` disabled:
- `GET /api/v1/meta/app/probe_gadget_app` → `200`, and the app is served;
- `GET /api/v1/meta/app` → the list omits it (5 → 4 items).

**Filed by** the `domain:engine` seat 1 (seat post #6367) · `os-project-manager` · session `session_01JtSQQ3EWsbNPzyYMug1tXy`, from the report above, as ruling item 7 of 6236971888 on #24097 directed. ⛔ Not a claim; the grade and lane are triage's.

**Reader who acts:** the seat that owns `packages/metadata-protocol` (`domain:engine` by the lane table), once triage grades it.

## Where (`origin/main`)

- `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts`: the list read (`readFlattenedMetaItems`) drops a disabled package's items for every type except `package` (`request.type !== 'package'` → `isPackageDisabled`). The by-name read falls through to the registry for every type, and serves them.
- #24097 (PR #24208) refuses the by-name read for `type: 'object'` only, with the data plane's `OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED` / `404`. That is the #7557 split: "Absence in the listing and refusal on the data plane are two halves of ONE answer" (`packages/objectql/src/package-disable-enforcement.test.ts`, docblock).
- So for `app`, `view`, `page`, `dashboard`, `flow` and every other non-package type, the by-name read and the list read still disagree about a disabled package's item.

## Open, to settle before choosing

- **The answer a non-object by-name read gives.** Objects have a data plane whose refusal code the by-name read now shares; other types have none. So it is absence (`404` not found) or a named refusal code. Today's ledger code is `OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED`, object-specific by name. A new or generalised code is a spec change (`domain:spec`).
- **The callers.** Which callers read a disabled package's non-object item by name for anything but using it (Studio, the console nav, authoring, migration)? #24097's dev measured the object callers. The non-object ones are not measured.

## Done when

- The by-name read and the list read give one answer for a disabled package's item of every non-package type. The chosen answer is pinned per type in the #7557 `READERS` table (an enumeration pin, so a new type cannot be missed).
- The doors that serve a by-name item answer the same: `RestServer`, the runtime dispatcher, `?layers=true`, and `/published` (the last is a code-read lead from #24097's report, not measured).

## Dedupe

MCP `search_issues` on this repository, closed included: `disabled package by-name meta read app view page served while list omits getMetaItem non-object type` gave 31 hits; the first 30 were read. #24097 is the object half (open, this family's first member). #18066 and #22614 are other by-name answer defects. #20193, #20237 and #20130 are per-caller gate gaps. #21817 and #21804 are package-axis list/by-name splits. None is the disabled-package by-name read of a non-object type.

Dedupe words: getMetaItem disabled package app served by name; by-name read disabled package non-object type; meta app by name list disagree disabled.
